controls.name: Central logging of organization-membership and GitHub installation changes
controls.description: The architecture states that ForgeFlow forwards application and security-relevant events to a shared logging platform, and lists 'Organization-membership changes' and 'GitHub installation changes' among the logged event types (evd-036). The security overview repeats that GitHub installation events and authentication activity are forwarded to the centralized logging platform (evd-131). This is a detective record that a membership or installation change occurred; no reviewed passage states that such an event causes a stored ForgeFlow membership record to be re-derived, nor that any alert or review is triggered, so the control observes the divergence rather than closing it.
controls.owner: ForgeFlow Platform Engineering / central logging platform team
limitations: The documents state that membership and installation change events are logged; they do not state that any process consumes them to update stored membership records (evd-036, evd-131).
No retention, review, or alerting behaviour for these specific event types is described (evd-131).

controls.name: Documented allocation of GitHub organization access management to the customer
controls.description: Product and integration documentation place responsibility for managing GitHub organization access, reviewing granted repository permissions, removing unused installations and maintaining GitHub identity and organization controls on the customer (evd-104, evd-069). The security overview records as an assumption that customer organizations appropriately manage GitHub permissions (evd-137). This allocates the upstream entitlement decision to the customer; it does not describe any ForgeFlow-side mechanism that reflects an upstream removal into the ForgeFlow membership records used for authorization (evd-027, evd-097).
controls.owner: Customer organizations (documented by ForgeFlow Product Management and Platform Engineering)
limitations: The customer's action takes effect on the GitHub side; no reviewed passage states that it propagates to the ForgeFlow membership and role records that authorize API access (evd-027, evd-097, evd-124).
Recorded as an assumption rather than an enforced property (evd-137).

mappings.applicability_reason: The threat's first step is a user authenticating through GitHub as an individual, and the requirement's applicable condition 'user authentication is delegated to an external identity provider' holds: ForgeFlow delegates customer authentication to GitHub and keeps no local password database (evd-027, evd-097).

ForgeFlow serves multiple customer organizations whose records share a single managed database (evd-032, evd-102), and this threat is precisely a request being evaluated against organization membership held server-side (evd-124), so both applicable conditions hold.
mappings.suppressed_conclusion: That tenant-aware authorization is absent or inadequate because no enforcement point (data access layer, middleware, or datastore constraint) is named and internal authorization implementation is intentionally omitted (evd-032, evd-138). The requirement remains live but the negative inference is not available from that silence.
mappings.suppressed_by: absent description of an authorization library or framework
assumptions: Proceeding on the basis that the 'organization context' carried on API requests operating on customer resources (evd-026) is the same context the authorization rules evaluate; no passage states whether it is derived from the session or supplied by the client.

mappings.applicability_reason: The requirement's conditions hold for the platform generally — artifacts from multiple customers share managed object storage under a documented, predictable path template (evd-033, evd-078) — but it bears on this threat only through the artifact-link step of the attack path (evd-046, evd-026), and separation by ForgeFlow organization does not address a reader whose ForgeFlow membership record still names that organization.
mappings.suppressed_conclusion: That artifact separation is inadequate because the paths are predictable and object-storage authorization enforcement is a named documentation gap (evd-033, evd-054). Logical separation is documented; whether it is enforced on access is unestablished rather than shown absent.
mappings.suppressed_by: absent description of a physical separation mechanism where logical separation is enforced and documented
assumptions: Assuming the 'artifact links' in the attack path are the time-limited access links the API generates for stored artifacts (evd-026, evd-033); the threat does not name the storage component explicitly.

mappings.applicability_reason: Installation events and installation permission updates are among the webhook types ForgeFlow subscribes to (evd-062), so the requirement engages this threat only if those inbound events are what would re-derive or revoke stored membership and installation state; no reviewed passage says they are used that way, so the condition cannot be established.
mappings.suppressed_conclusion: That origin authenticity of installation-related webhook events is not verified, because the documents say only that incoming requests are 'validated' (evd-028, evd-062, evd-128) and detailed webhook-validation behaviour is a named gap (evd-054).
mappings.suppressed_by: documentation stating only that requests are validated, where the mechanism is unstated

mappings.applicability_reason: The non-applicable condition 'authentication and its factor policy are entirely owned by an external provider and documented as such' holds for the actors in this threat: customer users and customer administrators authenticate through GitHub, which owns any factor policy, and ForgeFlow stores no passwords (evd-123, evd-097, evd-027). The administrative identity platform where MFA is recorded (evd-143) is not on this attack path.

The requirement's conditions concern operators acting through an administrative or operator interface. This threat's actors are customer users and customer administrators reading organization data through the customer API after a GitHub-side entitlement change (evd-097, evd-124, evd-046); the path does not traverse the internal administrative interface (evd-035).

The requirement applies to actions taken through a privileged operator interface. No step of this attack path is an operator action; the access occurs through ordinary customer API requests evaluated against stored membership (evd-124, evd-046), so the requirement's applicable conditions are not engaged by this threat.

This requirement concerns the breadth of privileges ForgeFlow requests from GitHub. The threat does not turn on that scope: worker repository access is obtained per operation as a short-lived installation-scoped token that follows current GitHub selection (evd-061, evd-065), while the disclosure occurs against ForgeFlow-held records read through the customer API (evd-124, evd-046).

The requirement's conditions concern data at rest and data crossing a network boundary the system does not control. In this threat the data is retrieved over an ordinary authenticated TLS session by a party the system's own records treat as a member (evd-126, evd-046), so transport and at-rest encryption are not the controls the threat defeats.

The requirement concerns removing customer data when a customer or operator requires it (evd-026, evd-096). This threat concerns continued read access by a user whose upstream entitlement was withdrawn while the data remains legitimately retained for the organization, so the requirement's conditions are not what the attack path engages.

documentation_gaps.title: Whether ForgeFlow membership and role records are re-derived from GitHub is not documented
documentation_gaps.description: The architecture states that after the GitHub flow completes ForgeFlow associates the GitHub identity with a ForgeFlow user and one or more customer organizations, and that organization membership and role information are stored in ForgeFlow (evd-027); authorization is then evaluated against those stored records (evd-097, evd-124). Installation events and installation permission updates are subscribed webhook types (evd-062) and membership and installation changes are logged (evd-036), but no reviewed passage states whether any of these re-derive, refresh, or revoke a stored membership record when a customer removes a user from the GitHub organization or reduces repository coverage (evd-058, evd-104). The security overview records internal authorization implementation among intentionally omitted details (evd-138). Trace cannot determine whether a synchronization or revocation control exists.
documentation_gaps.importance: Whether stored membership tracks GitHub-side reality determines whether a former GitHub organization member retains read access to structured analysis results and artifact links for that organization. The answer changes the satisfaction assessment of tenant-aware authorization for this threat and is obtainable from engineering documentation.
requested_evidence: Documentation describing how and when ForgeFlow organization membership and role records are created, refreshed, and removed relative to GitHub organization membership
A statement of whether installation, installation-permission, or membership webhook events cause membership or installation records to be updated or revoked
A description of the authorization model stating whether membership is read from stored records only, or re-checked against GitHub at authorization time

documentation_gaps.title: Customer session lifetime, renewal and revocation behaviour is not described
documentation_gaps.description: The architecture states only that 'the application uses secure browser sessions for subsequent customer requests' (evd-027), and the product and security documents describe sessions as established after successful GitHub authentication without further detail (evd-059, evd-123). Administrative sessions are documented as expiring after inactivity (evd-087), but no equivalent statement covers customer sessions, and no passage describes how a session is invalidated when membership or entitlement changes. Trace cannot determine whether a session-side control bounds the window in this threat.
documentation_gaps.importance: If stored membership is refreshed only at login, session lifetime and revocation determine how long an existing session continues to authorize access after a GitHub-side removal. The answer is obtainable and bears directly on the exposure window.
requested_evidence: Documentation stating customer session lifetime, idle expiry, and renewal behaviour
A description of how and when a customer session can be invalidated, including on membership or role change

documentation_gaps.title: The enforcement point for organization-scoped authorization is not identified
documentation_gaps.description: Customer-associated records carry an organization identifier and 'application services are responsible for applying organization-aware access rules when querying customer data' (evd-032); API requests operating on customer resources 'include an organization context' (evd-026). No reviewed passage names where the rule is enforced (shared data access layer, middleware, or datastore constraint) or whether the organization context is derived from server-side session state or accepted from the request, and the security overview places internal authorization implementation among intentionally omitted details (evd-138). Detailed tenant-isolation tests are a named architecture gap (evd-054).
documentation_gaps.importance: Without the enforcement point, Trace cannot verify req-AUTHZ-001 for this threat, and cannot distinguish an enforced boundary from a naming convention. The information is held in engineering documentation and would settle the mapping.
requested_evidence: Architecture or engineering documentation naming the component that enforces organization scoping on customer data queries
A statement of whether the organization context on an API request is derived from server-side session state or supplied by the client
Results or description of tenant-isolation tests referenced as a gap in evd-054

catalog_gap_candidates.concern: The catalog contains no requirement covering the currency of entitlements derived from an external identity or platform provider: that is, whether locally stored membership, role, or installation records are re-derived or revoked when the upstream grant they were derived from is withdrawn, and whether existing sessions are re-evaluated when that happens. ForgeFlow authenticates through GitHub but authorizes against membership and roles it stores itself (evd-027, evd-097, evd-124), while GitHub-side membership and repository selection change independently under customer control (evd-058, evd-104). Nothing in the catalog asks for the de-provisioning path to be documented.

nearest_requirements.why_not: It asks that the delegation, the provider, and the boundary of the provider's responsibility be documented. ForgeFlow documents all three (evd-027, evd-123); the requirement says nothing about keeping locally stored entitlements in step with the provider after the initial authentication.

It asks that every request be constrained to the tenant it belongs to and that tenant context be server-derived. A stale membership record satisfies that requirement exactly — the request is constrained to the organization the record names — while still authorizing a user whose upstream entitlement has been withdrawn.

It governs the scope of privileges the system requests from an external platform, not the lifecycle of a user's entitlement to the system's own data; the threat here is unaffected by how narrow the GitHub App's permissions are (evd-060, evd-065).
It concerns restriction and reach of an operator interface; the stale entitlement here belongs to an ordinary customer user acting through the customer API (evd-097, evd-046).
